incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected: sustained paging + OOM pressure on gpu-pool-03. Metric: node_paging_rate > 80% for 3m. Likely root: KV cache growth after recent int8 kernel selector change. thread_ts=1879123456
Sara L.: seeing same in dashboards — kv_cache_size jumped ~4x on several replicas after rolling to awq-int8 kernels at 03:05 UTC.
Miguel R.: confirmed. perf cliff on long-context chat models, throughput dropped and latency spiked. Some requests returned 503s when KV eviction couldn't keep up.
Ana K.: customer-facing impact: ~12 tenants saw >200ms p50 increase, 3 tenants hit transient 5xx for model servings. CX alerted.
Cheng W.: quick log dump from affected pod:```
[03:18:07] kv_cache: alloc 1.9G -> 7.6G (quantized path int8/awq)
[03:18:07] evict: candidate_scan_time 12ms -> 480ms
[03:18:07] batcher: inflight_batches 48 -> 240
[03:18:08] oom_killer_invoked false
[03:18:09] paging_rate 0.82
```
Kai T.: hypothesis: kernel selection changed to an awq-int8 variant that stores larger KV entries (padding/align differences). The runtime then increased prefix KV footprint and continuous batching kept appending into cache -> blowup.
Victor P.: can we temporarily pin model to fp16 path or revert kernel selector? Need a fast mitigation rather than fleet-wide rollback.
Miguel R.: suggested mitigations: 1) throttle continuous-batching (reduce max_batch_size and max_latency) 2) bump kv eviction aggressiveness 3) pin model variant to fp16 for high-traffic routes 4) scale up pool to buy breathing room.
Sara L.: I can apply a config hotfix to the route: set continuous_batch.max_batch_size=8 (was 64) and continuous_batch.max_latency_ms=5 (was 25) for affected model tags. This will reduce inflight batches and slow KV growth.
Ana K.: please coordinate with deploy-bot for safe rollout and let CX know estimated time to mitigation (eta ~10-15m).
deploy-bot: deploying route-config patch to 18/42 delegates (canary) ...
Miguel R.: also prepare an immediate kernel selector override: set model_catalog.<model>.quant_path_force=fp16 for the high-throughput alias. That forces runtime to use the float16 kernels without touching model weights. Low risk.
Cheng W.: applied eviction tuning on gpu-pool-03: kv.eviction.threshold=0.65 -> 0.45 and eviction.scan_window=128 -> 64. Watching memory reclaim.
Kai T.: rolling the route config hotfix to 100% now. If we see customer impact drop, keep until we have a proper kernel fix.
Sara L.: update: after canary (18 delegates) p99 latency dropped ~35% and paging_rate fell from 0.82 -> 0.34. No new 5xx counts in canary. Proceeding fleet-wide.
Victor P.: making public-facing note: short blip for some tenants, mitigation in progress, engineering investigating root cause (int8 kernel selection -> larger KV footprint). Drafted message for CX: "We observed transient latency increases due to a quantized kernel change increasing in-memory KV sizes. We rolled a route-level config hotfix and are monitoring; no data loss."
Miguel R.: simultaneous task: collect a stratified sample of KV entries for int8/awq/gptq paths to compare serialized sizes. We'll need to repro locally with the same kernel selection logic.
Cheng W.: added trace flags and a small repro harness pinned to the offending kernel. Will run against long-context test corpus.
Ana K.: CX updated, legal looped in for high-visibility customers. We should keep them informed every 30 minutes until stabilized.
Kai T.: next steps for permanent fix: either adjust kernel packer to reduce KV padding for awq/int8, or modify runtime KV layout for quant paths. Which one is lower risk?
Miguel R.: short term: kernel selector revert + runtime patch to normalize KV serialization for quant paths (small code change). Long term: add unit/regression for KV footprint on quant paths and a canary that measures kv_cache_delta after kernel changes.
Sara L.: escalated to eng-runtime for kernel rework. Can someone take ownership for the patch and postmortem?
Victor P.: I'll own the postmortem and follow-up action items (regressions: add canary alert, require kv-size bench in kernel PRs).
Miguel R.: on-call handoff: I'm stepping off in 20m. Kai please take over monitoring and final rollback authority if things regress.
Kai T.: taking on-call. watching liveliness. set alert: paging_rate > 0.5 -> page on-call immediately.
Sara L.: final note: incident status -> MITIGATED (config hotfix + eviction tuning + partial scaling). Monitoring for 2 hours. Opening incident ticket INV-1879123456.
incident-bot: Incident MITIGATED by Sara L., Miguel R., Cheng W., Kai T., Victor P.. See incident ticket: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INV-1879123456 :white_check_mark:
Victor P.: assigning follow-ups: (1) kernel KV serialization fix (owner: eng-runtime) (2) canary for kv-size after kernel flips (owner: eng-sre) (3) customer RCA note (owner: Victor P.). Will share draft in postmortems channel.
Miguel R.: thanks everyone. Good mitigation work. :thumbsup:
Kai T.: taking watch. please @me for any paging alerts.
Sara L.: handing off final logs and sample dumps to Victor. Good job team.
